details: Bitcoin surged above $80,000 for the first time since mid-May, extending a weekly rally of approximately 24%. This significant ascent is primarily attributed to robust institutional demand, evidenced by substantial inflows into spot Bitcoin ETFs, totaling $2.26 billion over six days. Further impetus came from the US Treasury's announcement of an expanded long-dated bond buyback program and a broader market shift towards risk-on sentiment.
title: Bitcoin Crosses $80K, Driven by ETF Inflows & US Treasury

details: Analysts at Bernstein are projecting Bitcoin targets of $150,000 by mid-2027 and a remarkable $300,000 by 2029. They argue that the escalating US government debt, which recently surpassed $40 trillion, is now a crucial catalyst. This "debasement trade," spurred by the Treasury's bond buybacks, is anticipated to compel investors towards scarce assets like Bitcoin and gold as a hedge against potential dollar devaluation.
title: US Debt Drives Bitcoin to Potential $300K Target by 2029

details: US spot Solana ETFs have achieved a new milestone, reaching cumulative net inflows of $1.22 billion. A significant portion of this, $33.5 million, flowed in on August 24 alone, marking the largest single-day inflow of 2026. This surge in institutional demand coincides with Solana (SOL) breaking above $100 after a 35% weekly rally, with additional bullish sentiment from ongoing discussions among validators to significantly increase token burns.
title: Solana ETFs Hit Record $1.22B Inflows; SOL Breaks $100

details: Hackers exploited a five-year-old firmware flaw in Coinkite's Coldcard hardware wallets, resulting in the theft of approximately $130 million worth of Bitcoin. The vulnerability compromised the seed phrase generation, enabling attackers to reconstruct private keys without physical access to the devices. This incident has raised concerns and negatively impacted public trust in the security of hardware wallets.
title: Coldcard Hardware Wallet Hack Steals $130M in Bitcoin
